title: Smoldering myeloma presenting as progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy: a case report
case_prompt: A 76-year-old woman presented with acute paresthesia of the left hand and face. Examination revealed left-sided hemiparesis with hypoesthesia and hypoalgesia, accompanied by neuropsychological symptoms. Noncontrast head CT showed no acute ischemia or hemorrhage. Initial brain MRI demonstrated a subcortical lesion in the right hemisphere, interpreted as a lacunar infarct. Despite standard treatment for cerebral ischemia, her hemiparesis progressed, and she was transferred to a neurology unit. Repeat MRI showed new T2-weighted hyperintense lesions in the right thalamus and left subcortical regions, while other periventricular and subcortical white-matter lesions remained unchanged. Diffusion-weighted imaging revealed abnormal diffusion in the right thalamus. On T1-weighted postgadolinium imaging, many lesions—both old and new—showed patchy, faint enhancement not present on the initial study. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed mild pleocytosis and elevated protein. CSF studies excluded bacterial meningoencephalitis, Lyme disease, tick-borne encephalitis, Herpes-simplex virus types 1 and 2, and Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Lacunar infarction considered because of the initial subcortical lesion, but was excluded when “hemiparesis was progressive despite standard treatment for cerebral ischemia.”  
2. Bacterial meningoencephalitis was excluded by CSF examination: “A cerebrospinal fluid examination excluded bacterial meningoencephalitis….”  
3. Lyme disease was ruled out: “…excluded … Lyme disease…”  
4. Tick-borne encephalitis was ruled out: “…excluded ... tick-borne encephalitis…”  
5. Herpes-simplex virus infection was excluded: “…excluded ... Herpes-simplex-virus 1 and 2…”  
6. Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease was excluded: “…and Creutzfeld-Jacob Disease.”  
7. Toxoplasmosis or lymphoma considered, typically requiring biopsy: “In some cases a biopsy may be necessary to either make a definite diagnosis or rule out other diseases, such as toxoplasmosis or lymphoma.”  
8. Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy was confirmed by detection of JC virus DNA: “PCR test for JCV-DNA was performed which revealed 4500 copies of JCV-DNA/ml in her cerebrospinal fluid.”
